questions.quesText: In Von Neumann architecture, which unit is responsible for executing arithmetic operations and logical decisions?
questions.explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs fundamental arithmetic operations (addition, subtraction) and bitwise/logical comparisons in the CPU.

questions.quesText: The average time complexity of searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree is ____.
questions.explanation: In a balanced BST (such as an AVL or Red-Black Tree), each comparison cuts the remaining search space in half, resulting in O(log n) time complexity.

questions.quesText: Von Neumann architecture uses separate physical memory spaces and buses for instructions and data.
questions.explanation: False. Harvard architecture uses separate memory spaces and buses for instructions and data. Von Neumann architecture shares a single memory space and bus system for both.

questions.quesText: In digital number systems, the base or radix of the hexadecimal number system is ____.
questions.explanation: The hexadecimal number system uses base 16, comprising digits 0-9 and letters A-F.

questions.quesText: The two's complement representation of a negative integer can be obtained by taking its one's complement and adding 1.
questions.explanation: True. In binary arithmetic, Two's Complement = One's Complement + 1.

questions.quesText: In standard flowchart notation, an oval or rounded rectangle represents a ____ symbol.
questions.explanation: An oval or rounded rectangle indicates the start or end (terminator) point of an algorithm in a flowchart.

questions.quesText: A recursive function without a base case will eventually trigger a stack overflow error at runtime.
questions.explanation: True. Each recursive call consumes a call stack frame. Without a terminating base case, the stack memory is exhausted.
